title: Safe money that shrinks
topic: Inflation and what your money can buy

steps.title: Your balance and what it can buy
steps.body: Prices go up over time. This is called [[inflation]]. In 10 years, prices can rise by about a third. Then €10,000 buys only what about €7,400 buys today. The balance in a savings account does not fall. But if prices rise faster than the interest the account pays, the money buys less each year.

steps.prompt: The chart shows how much savings can buy over the years. Move the interest slider. Find the interest rate where the money keeps the same buying power.

output.label: Change in what the money can buy

goal.hint: The interest must be at least as high as the price rise.

steps.prompt: Prices rise by 3% each year. A savings account pays 0.5% each year. After 10 years, how much less can €18,000 buy than today?
steps.reveal: About 22% less. The balance grows to about €18,900. Prices grow faster, so the money buys what about €14,000 buys today.

steps.prompt: True or false: money in a savings account cannot lose value.
steps.explanation: False. The balance does not fall, but prices rise. If the interest is lower than the price rise, the money buys less each year. The difference between interest and price rise is the [[real-return]].

steps.prompt: An account pays 1% a year. Prices rise by 3% a year. What happens to the money?
options: The balance grows, but it buys about 2% less each year
Nothing, because the balance never falls
The balance falls by 3% each year
steps.explanation: The balance rises by 1%. Prices rise by 3%. So the money buys about 2% less each year, even though the number on the screen goes up.

steps.title: What your savings can buy
steps.body: You have **{savingsBalance}** in your savings account. It pays **{savingsRate}** interest a year. If prices rise by 3% a year, your savings buy a little less each year.

steps.prompt: Your savings account pays {savingsRate} a year. Move the sliders to see what your savings can buy after some years, with different price rises.

output.label: Change in what your savings can buy

goal.hint: Move a slider to see the result change.

steps.note: The interest slider starts at your real rate. This is an example, not a forecast.

scenes.title: Same balance, higher prices
scenes.desc: Prices go up over time. This is called [[inflation]]. Your balance does not fall, but after 10 years the same money buys less.
